# FIX-ORI-AI-001-1: Keep the worked example hook's regenerate payload itemIds unique

## What this does

Fixes the worked example's retry defect at its root. After owned-endpoint loss, the `useLiveChat` hook's clearError-then-regenerate path assembles an outgoing payload containing duplicated assistant message entries that carry repeated OpenAI itemIds in `providerMetadata`; the real OpenAI Responses endpoint rejects that payload and the server emits an error record with 0 deltas. The fix keeps every assistant provider-metadata itemId unique across the outgoing history before the transport serializes the request body.

## Why

ORI-RN-004's cycle-1 blocked report (checkpoint a86231aa) root-caused the iOS/Android retry-completion failure headlessly with the hook's exact SDK classes (`Chat` from @ai-sdk/react 4.0.92 + `DefaultChatTransport` from ai 7.0.89, throttle 50) and bisected it on the real backend: any payload variant leaving each itemId unique completes. Web passes only because its fresh-session path never regenerates with stale history. No pending task owns the hook file — ORI-RN-004's write-allowlist cannot reach `apps/example/lib/use-live-chat.ts`, and ORI-AI-001 is completed — while the gate's locked steps already promise retry completion. The missing piece is this hook-side fix.

## How to verify

Run `pnpm exec tsx tests/sprint-05-orient-search/support/live-chat-regenerate-payload.test.ts` against the real owned backend and the official OpenAI Responses endpoint. The driver imports the real `Chat` + `DefaultChatTransport` classes from apps/example's installed packages, reproduces the endpoint-loss retry state through the owned backend lifecycle, captures the outgoing bodies and the server's sanitized records, and proves functional RED before the fix and GREEN after. Also run the preserved scoped compiler command below.

## Scope

Own the regenerate-payload fix in `apps/example/lib/use-live-chat.ts`, one new scoped driver under `tests/sprint-05-orient-search/support/`, and bounded evidence under `.tmp/FIX-ORI-AI-001-1/`. Rendered retry acceptance on devices remains with ORI-RN-004; the server, the screen and the native drivers stay untouched.

### SPECIFICATION

Remediate the ORI-AI-001 hook so the regenerate path emits provider-acceptable history. The defect: after a failed turn (endpoint loss), the outgoing regenerate payload contains duplicated assistant entries carrying repeated OpenAI itemIds in providerMetadata; the OpenAI Responses endpoint rejects it. The fix is a hook-level sanitize/stabilize of the outgoing history at the transport seam in `apps/example/lib/use-live-chat.ts`. Dependency installation ownership and the server stay with ORI-AI-001's landed surface; this task changes only the hook and adds one scoped driver.

### BOUNDARY CONTRACTS

1. Fix the root cause in `apps/example/lib/use-live-chat.ts`: keep every assistant provider-metadata itemId unique across the outgoing (regenerate) history before the transport serializes the body. The installed `HttpChatTransport` accepts `prepareSendMessagesRequest({ id, messages, trigger, messageId })` and returns the prepared request body (apps/example/node_modules/ai/src/ui/http-chat-transport.ts, lines 106-158) — pass it to the existing `new DefaultChatTransport({ api, fetch, ... })` construction; an equivalent transport-level sanitize inside the hook module is acceptable. Editing the server is not.
2. Sanitize semantics: keep the first occurrence of each itemId and strip the stale duplicates, or an equivalent uniqueness-preserving transform. Never invent provider itemIds, never remove message text, parts, or legitimate unique metadata.
3. Preserve the public hook contract from ORI-AI-001 AC-4: `messages`, `status`, `error`, `sendMessage`, `stop`, `regenerate`, `clearError`; retry makes 2 ordered calls `clearError()` then `regenerate()`; throttle 50; 0 initial messages; stable `DefaultChatTransport` with `expo/fetch`; absolute `EXPO_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL` validation appending `/api/chat`.
4. The scoped driver must exercise the REAL `Chat` + `DefaultChatTransport` classes resolved from the apps/example workspace packages (pnpm layout; ORI-RN-004 cycle-1 recorded that `ai` resolves only from apps/example's node_modules and its probes imported by absolute worktree path). The sanitize logic itself must live in and be exported from `apps/example/lib/use-live-chat.ts`. If the top-level `expo/fetch` import blocks headless import of the hook module outside Expo, a lazy dynamic import inside `chatFetch` is the allowed enabler — runtime behavior in Expo must stay identical.
5. Reuse `tests/sprint-05-orient-search/support/live-backend.ts` for backend launch/stop/restart; act only on recorded owned PIDs. The server emits sanitized records only at stream termination (apps/example/server/chat.ts finally block), so assertions await record emission rather than polling mid-stream.
6. Keep evidence under `.tmp/FIX-ORI-AI-001-1/` only, bounded and sanitized (request IDs, outcome, response IDs, delta counts, itemId-uniqueness results; never credentials or raw provider errors).

# Sprint 05: orient-search

**Status:** in_progress  
**Sequence:** 5  
**Timeline:** Phase 2

## Overview

Give a first-time integrator a complete orientation path: Introduction, one engine decision, registry-specific installation and CLI guidance, Theming and Dark mode, one seed-data Quickstart, and a handoff to a real AI SDK v7 example. Connect that content to persistent engine tabs, live theme values, built-site search, registry destinations, and useful missing-page recovery.

Absorb the smallest real prerequisites that make those paths executable: the published PromptInput import graph, both clean Expo consumers, a substantive ownership explanation, actual 404 recovery, the real example API and native composition, canonical registry hosting, and source-bound build and publication checks. This does not add another tutorial or a demonstrated use case. Sprint 06 may deepen the ownership tables; Sprint 11 may deepen resilience and accessibility; later delivery work may harden deployment and rollback.

The plan contains **36 tasks / 131 points**, compared with the roadmap sketch of approximately 12 items / 34–55 points: **76 points above its upper bound**. It retains 13 locked flows, 13 numbered gate steps, and four post-integration journey proofs. Estimates describe the approved prerequisite absorption rather than forcing the work into the sketch.

All implementation, functional RED, product verification, hosted acceptance, and deployment proof are future work. This document records a plan, not a passing gate or release.

## Human Testing Gate

**Gate:** A stranger opening /docs/introduction over the built site's local preview can read in one pass that the library provides universal AI chat and agent UI components for React Native, that it is distributed as a copy-paste registry, and that it is not an npm package.

**Entrypoint:** docs site local preview — built dist served by astro preview (http://localhost:4321) or the pnpm e2e:docs webServer; route /docs/introduction

**Before:** The source snapshot at the planned source SHA already contains Theming and shared layout, header, table, and tab controls. Introduction, Installation, CLI, Dark mode, Quickstart, the ownership-boundary route, and a custom 404 route are absent in that inspected snapshot. Existing Theming content still needs engine-correct claims and the real paired TokenTable. These are planning observations from the source, not current browser results. Each owner must observe the actual functional failure before implementation; the stale roadmap claim that all of these controls are absent is not a RED oracle.

**Success state:** A visitor reads useful, source-backed bodies instead of empty shells, chooses the correct engine once, follows literal registry commands, reads the same information without JavaScript, sees live theme changes without a flash, and reaches real content through keyboard search or missing-page recovery. The single Quickstart reaches a visible seed-data screen and then a separately verified real-provider example. Acceptance also requires the discriminating build checks and fresh native, provider, public-registry, and hosted evidence specified below.

**Demonstrates:** UC-DOCS-01, UC-DOCS-02, UC-SHELL-02, UC-SHELL-01 (TokenTable half), UC-SHELL-03 (prose-persistence half)

**Fixed carryover:** UC-GEND-07 AC-2; TR-12 (full); CAP-DOCS-01 snippet/link build integration. Boundary, recovery, API, and publication work support this projection; they do not expand the demonstrated-use-case list.

# FIX-ORI-AI-001-1: Keep the worked example hook's regenerate payload itemIds unique

## What this does

Fixes the worked example's retry defect at its root. After owned-endpoint loss, the `useLiveChat` hook's clearError-then-regenerate path assembles an outgoing payload containing duplicated assistant message entries that carry repeated OpenAI itemIds in `providerMetadata`; the real OpenAI Responses endpoint rejects that payload and the server emits an error record with 0 deltas. The fix keeps every assistant provider-metadata itemId unique across the outgoing history before the transport serializes the request body.

## Why

ORI-RN-004's cycle-1 blocked report (checkpoint a86231aa) root-caused the iOS/Android retry-completion failure headlessly with the hook's exact SDK classes (`Chat` from @ai-sdk/react 4.0.92 + `DefaultChatTransport` from ai 7.0.89, throttle 50) and bisected it on the real backend: any payload variant leaving each itemId unique completes. Web passes only because its fresh-session path never regenerates with stale history. No pending task owns the hook file — ORI-RN-004's write-allowlist cannot reach `apps/example/lib/use-live-chat.ts`, and ORI-AI-001 is completed — while the gate's locked steps already promise retry completion. The missing piece is this hook-side fix.

## How to verify

Run `pnpm exec tsx tests/sprint-05-orient-search/support/live-chat-regenerate-payload.test.ts` against the real owned backend and the official OpenAI Responses endpoint. The driver imports the real `Chat` + `DefaultChatTransport` classes from apps/example's installed packages, reproduces the endpoint-loss retry state through the owned backend lifecycle, captures the outgoing bodies and the server's sanitized records, and proves functional RED before the fix and GREEN after. Also run the preserved scoped compiler command below.

## Scope

Own the regenerate-payload fix in `apps/example/lib/use-live-chat.ts`, one new scoped driver under `tests/sprint-05-orient-search/support/`, and bounded evidence under `.tmp/FIX-ORI-AI-001-1/`. Rendered retry acceptance on devices remains with ORI-RN-004; the server, the screen and the native drivers stay untouched.

### OUTCOME

After owned-endpoint loss, the worked example hook's Retry (clearError then regenerate) produces an outgoing payload whose assistant providerMetadata itemIds are all unique; the real OpenAI Responses endpoint accepts it and the server records a new completed, provider-correlated answer with exactly 1 retained user turn. The normal send/follow-up path is unchanged.

### CRITICAL CONSTRAINTS — Never

- Never expose OPENAI_API_KEY to client imports, EXPO_PUBLIC variables, install/compiler processes, command arguments or captured evidence. Credentials reach only the trusted launcher and the server child.
- Never mock the thing under test: no mocked Chat, transport, fetch, server or provider. Drive the REAL classes installed for apps/example (ai@7.0.89, @ai-sdk/react@4.0.92) against the REAL backend route and the REAL OpenAI Responses endpoint.
- Never satisfy retry by duplicating the user turn (re-sending via sendMessage), swallowing the error, retrying silently in a loop, or classifying an errored HTTP 200 stream as completed.
- Never weaken the consumer oracle: the fixed retry must deliver a new real request ID, a completed provider-correlated answer, and exactly 1 retained user turn.
- Never strip or rewrite legitimate unique itemIds or remove message text/parts such that contextual history breaks (the follow-up must still retain the nonce).
- Never write outside the exact allowlist: NOT apps/example/server/**, NOT ORI-RN-004's screen/driver files, NOT ORI-AI-001's or ORI-RN-004's evidence directories, NOT the planning-owned surface policy.
- Never upgrade dependencies by default. Only a pinned real version with evidence from the installed packages that no hook-level fix can work; never "latest", never a forced alias.

### DONE WHEN

- [ ] AC-1 proves functional RED (duplicated-itemId payload → real provider rejection, 0 deltas) and GREEN (unique itemIds → new real request ID, completed provider-correlated record, exactly 1 retained user turn) on the real stack.
- [ ] AC-2 proves the happy path, hook contract, scoped compiler and exact scope compliance are preserved.
- [ ] The exact selector and preserved commands pass; independent review confirms canonical functional RED, seeded evidence and no stubs.

### SPECIFICATION

Remediate the ORI-AI-001 hook so the regenerate path emits provider-acceptable history. The defect: after a failed turn (endpoint loss), the outgoing regenerate payload contains duplicated assistant entries carrying repeated OpenAI itemIds in providerMetadata; the OpenAI Responses endpoint rejects it. The fix is a hook-level sanitize/stabilize of the outgoing history at the transport seam in `apps/example/lib/use-live-chat.ts`. Dependency installation ownership and the server stay with ORI-AI-001's landed surface; this task changes only the hook and adds one scoped driver.

### BOUNDARY CONTRACTS

1. Fix the root cause in `apps/example/lib/use-live-chat.ts`: keep every assistant provider-metadata itemId unique across the outgoing (regenerate) history before the transport serializes the body. The installed `HttpChatTransport` accepts `prepareSendMessagesRequest({ id, messages, trigger, messageId })` and returns the prepared request body (apps/example/node_modules/ai/src/ui/http-chat-transport.ts, lines 106-158) — pass it to the existing `new DefaultChatTransport({ api, fetch, ... })` construction; an equivalent transport-level sanitize inside the hook module is acceptable. Editing the server is not.
2. Sanitize semantics: keep the first occurrence of each itemId and strip the stale duplicates, or an equivalent uniqueness-preserving transform. Never invent provider itemIds, never remove message text, parts, or legitimate unique metadata.
3. # Sprint 05: orient-search

**Status:** in_progress  
**Sequence:** 5  
**Timeline:** Phase 2

## Overview

Give a first-time integrator a complete orientation path: Introduction, one engine decision, registry-specific installation and CLI guidance, Theming and Dark mode, one seed-data Quickstart, and a handoff to a real AI SDK v7 example. Connect that content to persistent engine tabs, live theme values, built-site search, registry destinations, and useful missing-page recovery.

Absorb the smallest real prerequisites that make those paths executable: the published PromptInput import graph, both clean Expo consumers, a substantive ownership explanation, actual 404 recovery, the real example API and native composition, canonical registry hosting, and source-bound build and publication checks. This does not add another tutorial or a demonstrated use case. Sprint 06 may deepen the ownership tables; Sprint 11 may deepen resilience and accessibility; later delivery work may harden deployment and rollback.

The plan contains **36 tasks / 131 points**, compared with the roadmap sketch of approximately 12 items / 34–55 points: **76 points above its upper bound**. It retains 13 locked flows, 13 numbered gate steps, and four post-integration journey proofs. Estimates describe the approved prerequisite absorption rather than forcing the work into the sketch.

All implementation, functional RED, product verification, hosted acceptance, and deployment proof are future work. This document records a plan, not a passing gate or release.

## Human Testing Gate

**Gate:** A stranger opening /docs/introduction over the built site's local preview can read in one pass that the library provides universal AI chat and agent UI components for React Native, that it is distributed as a copy-paste registry, and that it is not an npm package.

**Entrypoint:** docs site local preview — built dist served by astro preview (http://localhost:4321) or the pnpm e2e:docs webServer; route /docs/introduction

**Before:** The source snapshot at the planned source SHA already contains Theming and shared layout, header, table, and tab controls. Introduction, Installation, CLI, Dark mode, Quickstart, the ownership-boundary route, and a custom 404 route are absent in that inspected snapshot. Existing Theming content still needs engine-correct claims and the real paired TokenTable. These are planning observations from the source, not current browser results. Each owner must observe the actual functional failure before implementation; the stale roadmap claim that all of these controls are absent is not a RED oracle.

**Success state:** A visitor reads useful, source-backed bodies instead of empty shells, chooses the correct engine once, follows literal registry commands, reads the same information without JavaScript, sees live theme changes without a flash, and reaches real content through keyboard search or missing-page recovery. The single Quickstart reaches a visible seed-data screen and then a separately verified real-provider example. Acceptance also requires the discriminating build checks and fresh native, provider, public-registry, and hosted evidence specified below.

**Demonstrates:** UC-DOCS-01, UC-DOCS-02, UC-SHELL-02, UC-SHELL-01 (TokenTable half), UC-SHELL-03 (prose-persistence half)

**Fixed carryover:** UC-GEND-07 AC-2; TR-12 (full); CAP-DOCS-01 snippet/link build integration. Boundary, recovery, API, and publication work support this projection; they do not expand the demonstrated-use-case list.

requirements.description: GIVEN the installed Chat and DefaultChatTransport classes (ai@7.0.89, @ai-sdk/react@4.0.92, throttle 50) driven headlessly against the owned backend and the real OpenAI Responses endpoint WHEN the hook's clearError-then-regenerate retry path runs after owned-endpoint loss THEN the outgoing payload keeps every assistant providerMetadata itemId unique and the provider completes a new provider-correlated record with exactly 1 retained user turn.
requirements.name: Regenerate recovery after endpoint loss

steps: Launch the owned backend through support/live-backend.ts, stop it via its lifecycle handle, submit a nonce turn through the real Chat + DefaultChatTransport to produce the sanitized endpoint-loss error and the retained user turn, then restart the same owned endpoint.

Capture the pre-fix regenerate request body and the server's sanitized records; run the hook's retry path (clearError then regenerate) and observe the real OpenAI rejection with an error record and 0 deltas as functional RED.
Apply the itemId-uniqueness fix in apps/example/lib/use-live-chat.ts and repeat the identical retry path against the same real stack.

must_not_observe: Repeated itemIds or duplicated assistant entries in any outgoing body (duplicated itemId count greater than 0), a second user message, 0 completed provider records for the retried turn, an empty (0-delta) retry stream, the error record's outcome staying error after retry, a canned or replayed answer, or credentials in any captured evidence.
must_observe: Functional RED is captured before the fix: the regenerate payload carries duplicated assistant entries with repeated providerMetadata OpenAI itemIds and the server emits an error record with 0 deltas.

After the fix every assistant providerMetadata itemId in the outgoing regenerate payload is unique (0 duplicated itemId values across the regenerate request body) and the payload contains exactly 1 user turn for the failed submission.

In this leg's records the server shows exactly 2 outcome=completed records (the fresh seed turn and the retried turn) and exactly 1 error record (the endpoint-loss turn); the retried request has a new real request ID distinct from the failed one, an actual provider response ID, usage and at least 2 nonempty text deltas.

would_fail_if: The regenerate payload still contains duplicated assistant entries or repeated OpenAI itemIds, the retry is satisfied by duplicating the user turn, or a mocked Chat/transport/fetch/provider stands in for the real stack.

scenario.verification_service: real Node 24 example HTTP server through support/live-backend.ts, installed ai@7.0.89 and @ai-sdk/react@4.0.92 classes, and the OpenAI Responses API at https://api.openai.com/v1 using gpt-4.1-mini-2025-04-14

requirements.description: GIVEN the fixed hook and the same real stack WHEN a fresh-session send and an SDK-history contextual follow-up complete and the scoped live-chat compiler runs THEN legitimate unique itemIds and history pass through unchanged, the follow-up retains the nonce, the compiler exits 0 and the public hook contract is unchanged.
requirements.name: Happy-path preservation and hook contract intact

steps: Send a fresh nonce-bearing turn and an SDK-history contextual follow-up that omits the nonce through the fixed hook path; capture both outgoing bodies and both server records.
Run pnpm --dir apps/example exec tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.live-chat.json and inspect the actual hook diff against the allowlist.

must_not_observe: Stripped unique itemIds, a lost nonce, 0 completed provider records for the follow-up, an empty (0-delta) stream, a changed hook surface, server or screen/driver edits, or writes outside the exact allowlist.
must_observe: The full driver run records exactly 3 outcome=completed records (the fresh nonce turn, the post-retry regenerated turn and the contextual follow-up) with 3 distinct real provider response IDs; the follow-up answer contains the literal nonce string, and every captured outgoing body shows 0 duplicated itemId values with each legitimate unique itemId unchanged.

The scoped live-chat compiler exits 0; the hook still exposes messages, status, error, sendMessage, stop, regenerate and clearError with retry as clearError() then regenerate(), throttle 50 and a stable DefaultChatTransport with expo/fetch.
The complete diff touches only apps/example/lib/use-live-chat.ts, the new scoped driver and .tmp/FIX-ORI-AI-001-1 evidence.

would_fail_if: The sanitizer strips or rewrites legitimate unique itemIds or history content, the contextual follow-up loses the nonce, the hook surface or retry ordering changes, the transport is stubbed or the provider response is mocked rather than reaching the real OpenAI Responses endpoint, a static canned answer satisfies the oracle without a new real request ID, or the scoped compiler regresses.

findings: The defect is two failure classes, not one: duplicated assistant entries repeating itemIds AND unique-but-stale itemIds from streams that never completed, where the second class returns OpenAI 400 'Item with id … not found' even with zero duplicates — proven by direct provider replay in .tmp/FIX-ORI-AI-001-1/cycle-1/diag-raw-provider-error.ts, and invisible in server records because sanitizeError collapses every provider failure to one generic string (apps/example/server/chat.ts:162).

Mechanism: @ai-sdk/openai responses defaults store to true and converts every assistant text part carrying providerMetadata.openai.itemId into a bare item_reference whose content is NOT sent (apps/example/node_modules/@ai-sdk/openai/src/responses/convert-to-openai-responses-input.ts:606-610), so a stale itemId simultaneously drops the partial text and fails the request.

The client-side staleness signal is part.state: aborted turns leave text parts stuck at 'streaming' while completed turns end 'done' — this is what the sanitize keys on and it is the only reliable client-side discriminator.

The minimal AC-1 scenario as written (seed turn, stop backend, submit, restart, retry) does NOT reproduce the failure — a single completed turn plus endpoint loss retries successfully even pre-fix; an aborted mid-stream turn (or equivalent state damage) between them is the prerequisite, which is why the driver adds the aborted-essay leg.

Static or even type-only imports of apps/example modules (the hook via expo/fetch, and the ai/@ai-sdk/react dist d.ts themselves) add global DOM augmentations (HTMLElement | SVGElement unions) to the root tsc program and break unrelated spec files — any future driver touching these packages must runtime-load via computed specifiers with structural surfaces.

The published expo/fetch entry (expo/fetch.js requiring ./src/winter/fetch/index) cannot resolve in plain Node at all; only Metro resolves it, and its types live under expo/build/winter/fetch — which is why the lazy-import enabler works for types but must never be called headlessly.
